cases.sentence: Весь в ___ измазан, а в руках – ножик…
cases.translation: He is smeared all over in snot, and in his hands there is a little knife.
cases.explain: «В» here answers «в чём?» — a state or covering rather than motion — and that use of «в» requires the prepositional: в соплях.

cases.translation: "It's me," answered Mithridates, king of Pontus.
cases.explain: The name is in apposition to «царь», which is the subject of «ответил», so both stand in the nominative.

cases.translation: Put the knife away, put it away, what for...?
cases.explain: «Убери» is a transitive imperative, so its direct object is accusative; нож is inanimate, so the accusative looks like the nominative.

cases.sentence: И рабочий ударил меня ___ по голове.
cases.translation: And the worker hit me on the head with his hammer.
cases.explain: The tool used to perform an action stands in the instrumental with no preposition: ударил молотом.

cases.translation: You yourself said it to the sick boy.
cases.explain: The person spoken to is the indirect object of «говорить», which takes the dative — and the adjective «больному» agrees with it.
«От», meaning movement away from something, always governs the genitive: от рельсов.

cases.sentence: Кто зарезал твоих ___ и вытоптал твой жасмин?
cases.translation: Who slaughtered your little birds and trampled down your jasmine?
cases.explain: Птичек is the direct object of «зарезал», so accusative; because birds are animate, the plural accusative is borrowed from the genitive form.

reading.ru: О! теперь узнал: это понтийский царь Митридат.
reading.question: Who comes out of the fog towards Venichka?
reading.explain: At first the figure only seems familiar — "Achilles, not Achilles" — and then Venichka recognises him as King Mithridates.

reading.question: When does Mithridates say his nose runs worst?
reading.explain: He says it happens on other days too, but never the way it does at the full moon.

reading.ru: Весь в соплях измазан, а в руках – ножик…
reading.question: What is Mithridates carrying when he appears?
reading.explain: Venichka notices at once that the snot-smeared figure has a knife in his hands.

reading.question: What does Mithridates say the knife is for?
options: For cutting bread on the platform
For defending himself from the worker
reading.explain: Asked why he has the knife, Mithridates answers that it is obviously for cutting Venichka.

reading.question: How does Venichka come out of the Mithridates dream?
options: He wakes up shaking all over with convulsions
He wakes up calm and rested
He does not wake up at all
He is woken by a passing train
reading.correct: He wakes up shaking all over with convulsions
reading.explain: The stabbing in his sides throws him about the platform until he wakes, all in spasms.

reading.ru: Вокруг – ничего, кроме ветра, тьмы и собачьего холода.
reading.question: What does Venichka find around him when he first wakes on the platform?
options: Nothing but wind, darkness and a bitter cold
A crowd of passengers waiting for a train
The worker and the peasant woman standing over him
reading.correct: Nothing but wind, darkness and a bitter cold
reading.explain: There is no one there — only wind, dark, cold and a drizzle he cannot explain.

reading.ru: И рабочий ударил меня молотом по голове, а потом крестьянка – серпом по…цам.
reading.question: Who attacks Venichka in the second dream?
options: The worker and the peasant woman from Mukhina's sculpture
reading.correct: The worker and the peasant woman from Mukhina's sculpture
reading.explain: The two giants from Mukhina's statue float out of the fog and strike him with the hammer and the sickle.

reading.ru: Если каждая пятница моя будет и впредь такой, как сегодняшняя, – я удавлюсь в один из четвергов!..
reading.question: What does Venichka threaten to do if every Friday turns out like this one?
options: Hang himself on one of the Thursdays
Move back to Moscow for good
reading.correct: Hang himself on one of the Thursdays
reading.explain: He says that if his Fridays go on like this, he will hang himself on some Thursday — before the Friday can arrive.

reading.question: Where does Venichka realise he actually is?
reading.explain: He has arrived at the place he was travelling to, but it greets him with cold, rain and convulsions.

reading.ru: Боже, где твой чемоданчик с гостинцами?..
reading.question: What does Venichka discover is missing when he tries to get up?
options: His little suitcase with the presents
reading.correct: His little suitcase with the presents
reading.explain: The suitcase held two glasses of nuts for the boy, «Василёк» sweets and the empty bottles — and it is gone.

reading.question: What does Venichka tell himself is the most important thing to do?
options: Find the person who did not meet him
Go back to Moscow at once
Count what money he has left
reading.explain: He urges himself to move away from the track, because trains run there constantly between Moscow and Petushki.

highlight.question: Which sentence finally names the figure who comes out of the fog?
sentences: «Это лихорадка, – подумал я. – Этот жаркий туман повсюду – от лихорадки, потому что сам я в ознобе, а повсюду жаркий туман».
А из тумана выходит кто-то очень знакомый, Ахиллес не Ахиллес, но очень знакомый.
О! теперь узнал: это понтийский царь Митридат.
Весь в соплях измазан, а в руках – ножик…
highlight.explain: The third sentence is where the vaguely familiar figure is identified as King Mithridates.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that Mithridates had been talking peaceably until that moment?
sentences: И как он переменился сразу! все говорил мирно, а тут ощерился, почернел – и куда только сопли девались? – и еще захохотал, сверх всего!
Потом опять ощерился, потом опять захохотал!
highlight.explain: The first sentence contrasts his earlier peaceful talk with the snarling and blackening that follow.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what Venichka found around him after he woke?
sentences: Но тут мне пронзило правый бок, потом опять левый, опять правый, – я успевал только бессильно взвизгивать, – и забился от боли по всему перрону.
Вокруг – ничего, кроме ветра, тьмы и собачьего холода.
«Что со мной и где я? почему это дождь моросит? Боже…»
highlight.explain: Only the third sentence lists what surrounds him: wind, darkness and bitter cold.

highlight.question: Which sentence contains Venichka's threat about what he will do on a Thursday?
sentences: Если каждая пятница моя будет и впредь такой, как сегодняшняя, – я удавлюсь в один из четвергов!..
Таких ли судорог я ждал от вас, Петушки? пока я добирался до тебя, кто зарезал твоих птичек и вытоптал твой жасмин?..
highlight.explain: The fourth sentence is the one where he threatens to hang himself on one of the Thursdays.
